notes:
Company notes and CRM log:
- Product: in-app AI assistant + search for product analytics (B2B SaaS).
- Started with Redwood Hosted API POC (Q4 2025). Hosted eval used for embeddings + chat; team impressed with prompt quality and streaming.
- Current ask: Dedicated POC to meet predictable throughput and EU data residency for a subset of customers. Mid-market procurement timeline (legal + security) typical 4-6 weeks.
- Performance targets: p95 token gen latency <120ms for short chat responses, sustained throughput target 100-150 RPS across multitenant endpoints; cost sensitivity = medium-high (aim to keep token cost ~$0.002–0.006).
- Model preferences: prefer curated open variants; interested in quantized model variants for cost (e.g., redwood-curie-q4, redwood-curie-q4-rt). Want to evaluate model-routing by workload.
- Security: must pass SOC2 security questionnaire, require KMS integration for customer keys, SAML SSO for admin access, audit logs retention 24 months for select enterprise customers, EU data residency for EEA tenants.
- POC ask (Dedicated): 4-week sandbox with dedicated GPU pool, canary rollout plan, routing & fallback exercises, and a pricing commit conversation for a 12-month reserved plan if POC SLOs met.

Canary + routing plan (from SE call 2026-02-18):
- Phase 0 (smoke): small integration test to validate VPC peering, KMS, and model loading (0% user traffic).
- Phase 1 (canary): 5% production traffic -> Dedicated pool in us-east-1 (ded-gpu-2x). Canaries run with redwood-curie-q4-rt (low-latency) for 24 hours. Telemetry: p50/p95 latency, error rate, token cost, model quality (sampled prompts).
- Phase 2 (ramp): 5% -> 25% -> 60% over 48–72 hours if canary metrics pass thresholds. Auto rollback triggers: error rate >1.5% absolute, p95 latency increase >40% over baseline, or quality regression flagged by QA evals.
- Fallback routing: primary -> Dedicated us-east-1; if Dedicated capacity exhausted or failover triggered, automated route to Hosted API in same region (lower-cost model variant) OR route to Dedicated eu-west-1 pool depending on customer residency. Fallback policies include token-cost guardrails and per-tenant routing.
- Model variant strategy: prefer quantized redwood-curie-q4 for steady-state; keep smaller open-3b variant as emergency fallback for degraded conditions. Use automatic KV cache warmup on dedicated pool during ramp.
- Rollback plan: immediate traffic cutback to Hosted API (zero-downtime goal) + preserve recent KV caches; rollback SLA window 15 minutes for canary, 1 hour for full routings. Post-rollback runbook: collect model traces, attach Fireflies call id, create support ticket INF-3121 if incident.

Recent timeline (CRM bullets):
- 2026-01-12: Intro call w/ AE Maya Chen + product demo (hosted).
- 2026-01-20: Hosted POC started (embeddings + chat) — internal eval by CS team.
- 2026-02-02: Hosted POC results: latency OK for small scale; need predictable capacity.
- 2026-02-18: Technical deep-dive w/ SE Omar Rahman (Fireflies ff_20260218_8421). Discussed Dedicated sizing, canary plan, KMS integration.
- 2026-02-25: Security team submitted SOC2 questionnaire; asked for audit log retention and data residency confirmations. (ticket SEC-2026-44)
- 2026-03-03: Draft Dedicated POC plan shared (Drive link).
- 2026-03-10: Pricing review call with AE + finance — leaning toward 12-month reserved if POC meets SLOs.

Next steps (short):
- Schedule VPC peering and KMS onboarding (infra + Redwood infra ops) — target week of 2026-03-17.
- Confirm Dedicated pool sizing and exact canary percent + metric thresholds — SE to provide config by 2026-03-14.
- Legal to finalize contract addendum re: rollback SLA and data residency.

Notes: customer uses third-party identity provider (Okta). Quote from PM: "We need a plan that lets us route traffic away from Dedicated fast — our SLAs are customer-facing."
